Ezekiel 25:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 25:2.text: “Son of man, set your face firmly against the sons of Ammon and prophesy against them,

Ezekiel 25:3.text: and say to Ammon’s sons, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord: Because you rejoiced over My holy things when they were profaned, over Israel’s land when it was devastated, and over Judah’s house when they went into captivity,

Ezekiel 25:4.text: therefore behold, I am handing you to the sons of Kedem as an inheritance. They will camp with their equipment in you and set their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruits and drink your richness.

Ezekiel 25:5.text: I will make Ammon’s city pastures for camels, and Ammon’s sons a pasture for sheep. You will recognize that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 25:6.text: For thus says the Lord: Because you clapped your hand and made noise with your foot, and rejoiced from your soul over Israel’s land,

Ezekiel 25:7.text: therefore I will stretch My hand against you, give you to plunder among the nations, utterly destroy you from the peoples and make you perish from the countries with destruction. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’

Ezekiel 25:8.text: Thus says the Lord: Because Moab said, ‘Behold, Israel’s and Judah’s house is like all the nations,’

Ezekiel 25:9.text: therefore behold, I am paralyzing Moab’s shoulder from its frontier cities, the choice land, the house of Asimouth above a spring of a coastal city.

Ezekiel 25:10.text: To Kedem’s sons, against Ammon’s sons, I have given them as an inheritance, so that no remembrance of Ammon’s sons may remain.

Ezekiel 25:11.text: I will exact vengeance upon Moab, and they will recognize that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 25:12.text: Thus says the Lord: Because Idumea acted in vengeance against Judah’s house, and they bore a grudge and exacted punishment,

Ezekiel 25:13.text: therefore thus says the Lord: I will stretch My hand against Idumea and utterly destroy human and animal from her. I will make her a wilderness, and those pursued from Thaiman will fall by the sword.

Ezekiel 25:14.text: I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 25:15.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Because the foreigners acted in vengeance and stirred up vengeance, rejoicing from their soul to wipe out for ever,

Ezekiel 25:16.text: therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will stretch My hand against the foreigners, utterly destroy Cretans and make the remaining inhabitants of the coast perish.

Ezekiel 25:17.text: I will execute great acts of vengeance upon them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring My vengeance upon them.”

Ezekiel 26:1.text: In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 26:2.text: “Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, ‘Well done! She is shattered; the nations have perished. She has turned to me; the full one has been laid waste,’

Ezekiel 26:3.text: therefore thus says the Lord: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea rises with its waves.

Ezekiel 26:4.text: They will throw down Tyre’s walls and throw down your towers. I will winnow her dust from her and make her a smooth rock.

Ezekiel 26:5.text: She will be a drying place for nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord. She will become plunder for the nations,

Ezekiel 26:6.text: and her daughters in the plain will be killed by the sword. They will know that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 26:7.text: For thus says the Lord: I am bringing against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north—he is king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, and an assembly of very many nations.

Ezekiel 26:8.text: He will kill your daughters in the plain with the sword, set an advance guard against you, build around you, and make a palisade and a ring of weapons around you; he will set his spears opposite you.

Ezekiel 26:9.text: He will throw down your walls and your towers with his swords.

Ezekiel 26:10.text: The dust of his multitude of horses will cover you, and your walls will shake at the sound of his horsemen and his chariots’ wheels when he enters your gates like someone entering a city from the plain.

Ezekiel 26:11.text: With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.

Ezekiel 26:12.text: He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.

Ezekiel 26:13.text: He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.

Ezekiel 26:14.text: I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 26:15.text: For thus says the Lord, the Lord, to Tyre: Will not the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and a sword is drawn within you?

Ezekiel 26:16.text: All the rulers from the nations of the sea will step down from their thrones, remove the turbans from their heads, and strip off their patterned clothing. They will be utterly astonished, sit on the ground, fear their own destruction, and groan over you.

Ezekiel 26:17.text: They will raise a lament over you and say to you: ‘How you were destroyed from the sea, praised city that spread her fear to all who live in her!

Ezekiel 26:18.text: The islands will be afraid from the day of your fall.’

Ezekiel 26:19.text: For thus says the Lord, the Lord: When I make you a desolated city like cities that will not be inhabited, when I bring the abyss up over you and much water covers you,

Ezekiel 26:20.text: I will bring you down to those descending into the pit, to the people of old. I will settle you in the depths of the earth like an everlasting wilderness, with those descending into the pit, so that you are not inhabited and do not rise in the land of life.

Ezekiel 26:21.text: I will bring you to ruin, and you will no longer exist for ever, says the Lord, the Lord.”

Ezekiel 27:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 27:2.text: “Son of man, take up a lament over Tyre,

Ezekiel 27:3.text: and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrance of the sea, the trading place of the peoples from many islands: Thus says the Lord to Tyre: You said, ‘I have clothed myself with my beauty.’

Ezekiel 27:4.text: In the heart of the sea, at Beelim, your sons clothed you with beauty.

Ezekiel 27:5.text: Cedar from Senir was built for you; strips of cypress planks were taken from Lebanon to make fir masts for you.

Ezekiel 27:6.text: From Bashan they made your oars; they made your sacred places from ivory, wooded houses from the islands of Kittim.

Ezekiel 27:7.text: Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt became your bedding, to clothe you with glory and wrap you in blue and purple from the islands of Elishah; it became your coverings.

Ezekiel 27:8.text: Your rulers who inhabit Sidon, and the Arvadites, became your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, who were in you, were your pilots.

Ezekiel 27:9.text: The elders of Byblos and their wise men were in you; they strengthened your counsel. All the ships of the sea and their rowers came to you toward the farthest west.

Ezekiel 27:10.text: Persians, Lydians, and Libyans were in your force; your warrior men hung small shields and helmets in you; they gave you your glory.

Ezekiel 27:11.text: Sons of Arvadites and your force were on your walls; guards were in your towers. They hung their quivers around your harbors; they completed your beauty.

Ezekiel 27:12.text: Carthaginians were your traders because of the abundance of all your strength; they gave silver, gold, iron, tin, and lead for your market.

Ezekiel 27:13.text: Greece, all of it, and the adjoining regions traded with you in human lives, and gave bronze vessels for your commerce.

Ezekiel 27:14.text: From the house of Togarmah they gave horses and horsemen for your market.

Ezekiel 27:15.text: Sons of Rhodians were your traders; from islands they increased your commerce with ivory tusks, and you gave your payments in exchange for the imported goods,

Ezekiel 27:16.text: people as your merchandise from the abundance of your mixed company, myrrh drops and embroideries from Tarshish; Ramoth and Chorchor gave for your market.

Ezekiel 27:17.text: Judah and the sons of Israel were your traders in the sale of grain, perfumes, and cassia; they gave choice honey, oil, and resin to your mixed company.

Ezekiel 27:18.text: Damascus was your trader because of the abundance of all your strength: wine from Helbon and wool from Miletus;

Ezekiel 27:19.text: and they gave wine for your market. From Asel, worked iron and a wheel are among your mixed company.

Ezekiel 27:20.text: Dedan was your trader with choice animals for chariots.

Ezekiel 27:21.text: Arabia and all the rulers of Kedar were your traders through your hand, with camels, rams, and lambs in which they traded with you.

Ezekiel 27:22.text: Traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders with choice spices and good stones, and they gave gold for your market.

Ezekiel 27:23.text: Haran and Channa were your traders; Asshur and Charman were your traders,

Ezekiel 27:24.text: bringing merchandise, blue cloth and choice treasures bound with cords, and cypress

Ezekiel 27:25.text: ships: in them Carthaginians were your traders in abundance among your mixed company. You were filled and became very heavy in the heart of the sea.

Ezekiel 27:26.text: Your rowers led you in much water; the south wind shattered you in the heart of the sea.

Ezekiel 27:27.text: There were your forces, your payment and that of your mixed companies, your rowers and pilots, your counselors and your mixed companies from your mixed companies, all your warrior men in you, and your whole assembly within you; they will fall in the heart of the sea on the day of your fall.

Ezekiel 27:28.text: At the sound of your cry, your pilots will be greatly afraid,

Ezekiel 27:29.text: and all your rowers will come down from the ships; the passengers and the lookouts of the sea will stand on the land.

Ezekiel 27:30.text: They will raise a cry over you with their voice and cry bitterly; they will put earth on their head and spread ashes beneath them.

Ezekiel 27:32.text: Their sons will take up a lament over you and a lamentation for you:

Ezekiel 27:33.text: ‘What a payment you found from the sea! You filled nations from your abundance, and from your mixed company you enriched all the kings of the earth.

Ezekiel 27:34.text: Now you were shattered in the sea, in the depth of water; your mixed company and all your assembly fell within you—all your rowers.

Ezekiel 27:35.text: All who inhabit the islands became gloomy over you; their kings were utterly astonished, and their faces shed tears.

Ezekiel 27:36.text: Traders from nations hissed at you; you came to ruin, and you will be no more for ever.’”

Ezekiel 28:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 28:2.text: “And you, son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the Lord: Because your heart was exalted and you said, ‘I am a god; I have inhabited a god’s dwelling in the heart of the sea’—yet you are a human, and not a god, and you made your heart like a god’s heart—

Ezekiel 28:3.text: Surely you are not wiser than Daniel? Did wise men not instruct you in their knowledge?

Ezekiel 28:4.text: Surely it was not by your knowledge or understanding that you built up strength for yourself, and gold and silver in your treasuries?

Ezekiel 28:5.text: By your abundant knowledge and your trade you increased your strength; your heart was exalted in your strength.

Ezekiel 28:6.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Since you made your heart like a god’s heart,

Ezekiel 28:7.text: therefore, behold, I am bringing foreigners against you, scourges from nations. They will draw their swords against you and against the beauty of your knowledge, and lay your beauty out for destruction,

Ezekiel 28:8.text: and they will bring you down; you will die the death of wounded men in the heart of the sea.

Ezekiel 28:9.text: Surely you will not say, ‘I am a god,’ before those killing you? You are a human, and not a god. In a multitude

Ezekiel 28:10.text: of uncircumcised people you will perish by foreigners’ hands, for I have spoken, says the Lord.”

Ezekiel 28:11.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 28:12.text: “Son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Tyre and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: You were a seal of likeness and a crown of beauty;

Ezekiel 28:13.text: you came to be in the delight of God’s paradise. You have been clothed with every good stone: carnelian, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, jasper, silver, gold, ligurite, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. You filled your treasuries and storehouses within you with gold from the day you were created.

Ezekiel 28:14.text: With the cherub I placed you on God’s holy mountain; you came to be among fiery stones.

Ezekiel 28:15.text: You were blameless in your days from the day you were created until wrongdoings were found in you.

Ezekiel 28:16.text: From the abundance of your trade you filled your store chambers with lawlessness, and you sinned and were wounded away from God’s mountain; the cherub led you out from among fiery stones.

Ezekiel 28:17.text: Your heart was exalted because of your beauty; your knowledge was corrupted together with your beauty. Because of your many sins I threw you to the ground; I placed you before kings to be made a spectacle.

Ezekiel 28:18.text: Because of your many sins and the wrongdoings of your trade you profaned your sacred places. I will bring fire out from within you; it will consume you. I will turn you to ashes on your land before all who see you.

Ezekiel 28:19.text: All who know you among the nations will become gloomy over you; you came to ruin, and you will no longer exist for ever.”

Ezekiel 28:20.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 28:21.text: “Son of man, fix your face upon Sidon and prophesy against her,

Ezekiel 28:22.text: and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you. You will know that I am the Lord when I execute judgments in you, and I will be sanctified in you.

Ezekiel 28:23.text: Blood and death will be in your broad streets, and wounded men will fall by swords in you, all around you. They will know that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 28:24.text: The house of Israel will no longer have a thorn of bitterness or a thorn of pain from all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 28:25.text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will gather Israel from the nations where they were scattered, and I will be sanctified in them before the peoples and the nations. They will dwell on their land, which I have given to My servant Jacob,

Ezekiel 28:26.text: and they will dwell on it in hope, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell in hope when I execute judgment on all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord their God and the God of their fathers.”

Ezekiel 29:1.text: In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 29:2.text: “Son of man, fix your face upon Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt,

Ezekiel 29:3.text: and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh, the great dragon seated among his rivers, who says, ‘The rivers are mine, and I made them.’

Ezekiel 29:4.text: I will put traps in your jaws and fasten the fish of your river to your fins. I will bring you up from the midst of your river, and all the fish of your river,

Ezekiel 29:5.text: and I will cast you down quickly, and all the fish of your river. You will fall on the face of the plain; you will certainly not be gathered or wrapped for burial. I have given you for food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven.

Ezekiel 29:6.text: All who inhabit Egypt will know that I am the Lord, because you became a reed staff for the house of Israel.

Ezekiel 29:7.text: When they took hold of you with their hand, you were crushed; and when every hand prevailed against them, and when they rested upon you, you were shattered and broke all their loins.

Ezekiel 29:8.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy humans and livestock from you.

Ezekiel 29:9.text: The land of Egypt will become a ruin and a wilderness, and they will know that I am the Lord, because you say, ‘The rivers are mine, and I made them.’

Ezekiel 29:10.text: Therefore, behold, I am against you and against all your rivers. I will make the land of Egypt a wilderness, a sword, and destruction, from Migdol and Syene as far as the borders of the Ethiopians.

Ezekiel 29:11.text: No human foot will pass through it, nor will livestock’s foot pass through it; it will not be inhabited for forty years.

Ezekiel 29:12.text: I will make her land a ruin amid desolated land, and her cities will be amid desolated cities for forty years. I will scatter Egypt among the nations and winnow them into the countries.

Ezekiel 29:13.text: Thus says the Lord: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations where they were scattered,

Ezekiel 29:14.text: and I will turn back the captivity of the Egyptians and settle them in the land of Pathros, in the land from which they were taken; it will be a lowly dominion

Ezekiel 29:15.text: among all the dominions; it will no longer be exalted over the nations, and I will make them few, so that they are not more numerous among the nations.

Ezekiel 29:16.text: They will no longer be a hope for the house of Israel, bringing lawlessness to remembrance when they follow after them. They will know that I am the Lord.”

Ezekiel 29:17.text: In the twenty-seventh year, on the first of the first month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 29:18.text: “Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon subjected his force to great servitude against Tyre; every head was bald and every shoulder was losing its hair. Yet neither he nor his force received wages for Tyre and the servitude they performed against her.

Ezekiel 29:19.text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take her booty and strip her spoils; it will be wages for his force.

Ezekiel 29:20.text: In exchange for his service, which he performed against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:

Ezekiel 29:21.text: On that day a horn will spring up for the whole house of Israel, and I will give you an opened mouth among them. They will know that I am the Lord.”

Ezekiel 30:1.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 30:2.text: “Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: Alas, alas, the day!

Ezekiel 30:3.text: For the Lord’s day is near; it will be a day, an end of nations.

Ezekiel 30:4.text: A sword will come upon the Egyptians, and there will be turmoil in Ethiopia; wounded men will fall in Egypt, and her foundations will collapse together.

Ezekiel 30:5.text: Persians, Cretans, Lydians, Libyans, all the mixed company, and some of the sons of My covenant will fall by the sword in her.

Ezekiel 30:6.text: Egypt’s supports will fall, and the arrogance of her strength will come down from Migdol to Syene; they will fall in her by the sword, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 30:7.text: She will be desolated among desolated countries, and their cities will be among desolated cities.

Ezekiel 30:8.text: They will know that I am the Lord when I put fire upon Egypt and all who help her are shattered.

Ezekiel 30:9.text: On that day messengers will go out, hastening to lay Ethiopia waste; turmoil will be among them on Egypt’s day, for behold, it is coming.

Ezekiel 30:10.text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the multitude of Egyptians by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,

Ezekiel 30:11.text: him and his people: scourges from nations sent to destroy the land. They will all draw their swords against Egypt, and the land will be filled with wounded men.

Ezekiel 30:12.text: I will make their rivers desolate and destroy the land and all that fills it by foreigners’ hands. I, the Lord, have spoken.

Ezekiel 30:13.text: For thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the magnates from Memphis and the rulers from the land of Egypt, and they will be no more.

Ezekiel 30:14.text: I will destroy the land of Pathros, put fire upon Tanis, and execute vengeance in Diospolis,

Ezekiel 30:15.text: and pour out My wrath upon Sais, Egypt’s strength, and destroy the multitude of Memphis.

Ezekiel 30:16.text: I will put fire upon Egypt; Syene will be greatly troubled, and in Diospolis there will be a breach, and waters will pour out.

Ezekiel 30:17.text: The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and the women will go into captivity.

Ezekiel 30:18.text: At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark when I shatter Egypt’s scepters there and the arrogance of her strength perishes there. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will be led away captive.

Ezekiel 30:19.text: I will execute judgment in Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord.”

Ezekiel 30:20.text: In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 30:21.text: “Son of man, I shattered the arms of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Behold, it has not been bound up to provide healing, to put a poultice upon it, to give strength to grasp a sword.

Ezekiel 30:22.text: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will shatter his arms, the strong and the outstretched, and cast his sword down from his hand,

Ezekiel 30:23.text: and scatter Egypt into the nations and winnow them into the countries.

Ezekiel 30:24.text: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put My sword into his hand; he will bring it upon Egypt, take her booty, and strip her spoils.

Ezekiel 30:25.text: I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall. They will know that I am the Lord when I put My sword into the hands of the king of Babylon and he stretches it over the land of Egypt.

Ezekiel 30:26.text: I will scatter Egypt into the nations and winnow them into the countries. All will know that I am the Lord.”

Ezekiel 31:1.text: In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 31:2.text: “Son of man, say to Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and to his multitude, ‘To whom did you liken yourself in your height?

Ezekiel 31:3.text: Behold, Assyria was a cypress in Lebanon, beautiful in offshoots and tall in size; its crown reached into the midst of clouds.

Ezekiel 31:4.text: Water nourished it; the abyss raised it high, led its rivers around its plantings and sent out its gatherings of water to all the plain’s trees.

Ezekiel 31:5.text: Therefore its size rose above all the plain’s trees, and its branches spread wide because of abundant water.

Ezekiel 31:6.text: All the sky’s birds nested in its offshoots; all the plain’s beasts gave birth beneath its branches, and every multitude of nations lived in its shade.

Ezekiel 31:7.text: It was beautiful in its height because of the multitude of its branches, for its roots reached abundant water.

Ezekiel 31:8.text: Such cypresses did not exist in God’s paradise; pines were not like its offshoots, and firs were not like its branches. No tree in God’s paradise resembled it in its beauty

Ezekiel 31:9.text: because of the multitude of its branches, and the trees of God’s paradise of delight envied it.

Ezekiel 31:10.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you became great in size and set your crown amid clouds, and I saw it being lifted high,

Ezekiel 31:11.text: I handed it into the hands of a ruler of nations, and he brought about its destruction.

Ezekiel 31:12.text: Foreigners, scourges from nations, utterly destroyed it and cast it upon the mountains. Its branches fell in all the ravines; its trunks were shattered in every plain of the land. All the nations’ peoples went down from their shelter and dashed it to the ground.

Ezekiel 31:13.text: All the sky’s birds rested upon its fallen trunk, and all the field’s beasts were upon its trunks,

Ezekiel 31:14.text: so that none of the trees in the water may rise high in their size. They did not set their crowns amid clouds, and none of those drinking water stood toward them in their height. All were given to death, to the depth of the earth, among human beings, with those descending to a pit.

Ezekiel 31:15.text: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: On the day it descended to Hades, the abyss mourned it. I stopped its rivers and restrained the multitude of water. Lebanon grew dark over it, and all the plain’s trees collapsed over it.

Ezekiel 31:16.text: At the sound of its fall the nations shook when I brought it down to Hades with those descending to a pit. In the earth all the trees of delight and the choice trees of Lebanon, all drinking water, comforted it.

Ezekiel 31:17.text: For they too went down with it to Hades among those wounded by the sword; its offspring, those living under its shelter, perished in the midst of their life.

Ezekiel 31:18.text: Whom were you likened to? Descend and be brought down with the trees of delight into the earth’s depth. Among the uncircumcised you will lie with those wounded by the sword. So it is with Pharaoh and the multitude of his strength, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 32:1.text: In the eleventh year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 32:2.text: “Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and say to him, ‘You were likened to a lion of nations, and you are like the dragon in the sea. You butted in your rivers, troubled water with your feet and trampled your rivers.

Ezekiel 32:3.text: Thus says the Lord: I will throw nets of many peoples over you and haul you up with My hook,

Ezekiel 32:4.text: and stretch you out upon the earth; plains will be filled with you. I will seat all the sky’s birds upon you and fill all the beasts of the whole earth with you.

Ezekiel 32:5.text: I will lay your flesh upon the mountains and fill them with your blood,

Ezekiel 32:6.text: and the earth will be watered from your discharges, from your multitude upon the mountains. I will fill ravines with you.

Ezekiel 32:7.text: When you are extinguished, I will cover heaven and darken its stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon certainly will not show its light.

Ezekiel 32:8.text: All the things shining light in heaven will grow dark over you, and I will put darkness upon your land, says the Lord, the Lord.

Ezekiel 32:9.text: I will provoke the heart of many peoples when I bring your captivity among the nations, into a land you have not known.

Ezekiel 32:10.text: Many nations will grow gloomy over you; their kings will be utterly astounded when My sword flies before their faces, awaiting their own fall from the day of your fall.

Ezekiel 32:11.text: For thus says the Lord: Babylon’s king’s sword will come upon you

Ezekiel 32:12.text: with giants’ swords, and I will strike down your strength. All are scourges from nations; they will destroy Egypt’s arrogance, and all her strength will be shattered.

Ezekiel 32:13.text: I will destroy all her livestock beside the abundant water. No human foot will ever trouble it again, nor will livestock’s tread trample it.

Ezekiel 32:14.text: Thus their waters will then become still, and their rivers will flow like oil, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 32:15.text: When I give Egypt to destruction and the land is made desolate with its fullness, when I scatter all who dwell in her, they will know that I am the Lord.

Ezekiel 32:16.text: It is a lament, and you will lament it, and the nations’ daughters will lament it. Over Egypt and all her strength they will lament her, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

Ezekiel 32:17.text: In the twelfth year, in the first month, on the fifteenth of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 32:18.text: “Son of man, lament over Egypt’s strength. The nations will bring her daughters down dead into the earth’s depth, with those descending to a pit.

Ezekiel 32:20.text: They will fall with him among those wounded by the sword, and all his strength will lie down.

Ezekiel 32:21.text: The giants will say to you, ‘Be in the depth of a pit! Whom do you surpass? Descend and lie with the uncircumcised among those wounded by the sword.’

Ezekiel 32:22.text: There Assyria and all his assembly, all wounded, were placed. Their burial is in the depth of a pit, and his assembly was around his tomb, all the wounded who fell by the sword,

Ezekiel 32:23.text: who spread their fear upon the land of life.

Ezekiel 32:24.text: There is Elam and all his force around his tomb, all the wounded who fell by the sword and those descending uncircumcised into the earth’s depth, who spread their fear upon the land of life and received their torment with those descending to a pit,

Ezekiel 32:26.text: There were placed Mosoch and Thobel and all their strength around his tomb, all his wounded, all uncircumcised, wounded by the sword, who spread their fear upon the land of life.

Ezekiel 32:27.text: They lay with the giants who fell long ago, who descended to Hades with weapons of war and put their swords beneath their heads. Their lawless deeds were upon their bones, because they terrified giants in the land of life.

Ezekiel 32:28.text: You too will lie among the uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword.

Ezekiel 32:29.text: There were placed Assyria’s rulers, who gave his strength to a sword wound. These lay with the wounded, with those descending to a pit.

Ezekiel 32:30.text: There are the north’s rulers, all Assyria’s generals, who descended wounded. With their fear and their strength they lay uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword and carried away their torment with those descending to a pit.

Ezekiel 32:31.text: King Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all their strength, says the Lord, the Lord.

Ezekiel 32:32.text: For I have set his fear upon the land of life, and he will lie among the uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword—Pharaoh and all his multitude—says the Lord, the Lord.”

Jeremiah 30:1.text: For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.

Jeremiah 30:2.text: Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.

Jeremiah 30:3.text: For grape gatherers came to you; they will leave you no remnants. Like thieves by night they will lay their hand upon you.

Jeremiah 30:4.text: For I dragged Esau away and uncovered their secrets; they certainly cannot hide. They perished by the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible

Jeremiah 30:5.text: for your orphan to remain so that he may live. And I will live, and widows have trusted in Me.

Jeremiah 30:6.text: For thus said the Lord: Those for whom there was no law to drink the cup drank it. And you, though acquitted, certainly will not be acquitted, for you will certainly drink.

Jeremiah 30:7.text: For I swore by Myself, says the Lord, that you will become an untrodden place, a reproach, and a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be deserted for ever.

Jeremiah 30:8.text: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent messengers to the nations: Gather and come against her; rise for war!

Jeremiah 30:9.text: I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.

Jeremiah 30:10.text: Your playfulness assailed you; your heart’s insolence destroyed holes in rocks and seized the strength of a high hill. For he raised his nest like an eagle; from there I will bring you down.

Jeremiah 30:11.text: Idumea will become an untrodden place; everyone passing by her will hiss.

Jeremiah 30:12.text: As Sodom, Gomorrah, and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, no person will settle there, and no human being will live there.

Jeremiah 30:13.text: Like a lion he will come up from Jordan’s midst into Aitham’s place, for I will quickly drive them away from her. Appoint the young men over her. For who is like Me? Who will resist Me, and what shepherd can stand before Me?

Jeremiah 30:14.text: Therefore hear the Lord’s counsel that He planned against Idumea and His purpose against Teman’s inhabitants: Surely the smallest sheep will be swept together; surely their dwelling will be made untrodden over her.

Jeremiah 30:15.text: For at the sound of their fall the earth shook, and your cry was heard at the sea.

Jeremiah 30:16.text: Like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications. That day Idumea’s strong men’s hearts will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

Obadiah 1:1.text: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God to Idumea: I heard a report from the Lord, and He sent a dispatch to the nations: “Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!”

Obadiah 1:2.text: Look, I have made you insignificant among the nations; you are greatly dishonored.

Obadiah 1:3.text: The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who camp in holes in the rocks, raising his dwelling high and saying in his heart, “Who will bring me down to the ground?”

Obadiah 1:4.text: If you soar like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.

Obadiah 1:5.text: If thieves came in to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen enough for themselves? And if grape gatherers came in to you, would they not have left a gleaning?

Obadiah 1:6.text: How Esau has been searched out, and his hidden things seized!

Obadiah 1:7.text: All the men of your covenant sent you out as far as your borders; the men at peace with you opposed you and prevailed over you. They set ambushes beneath you. There is no understanding in them.

Obadiah 1:8.text: On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the wise from Idumea and understanding from Mount Esau.

Obadiah 1:9.text: Your warriors from Teman will be terrified, so that a person may be removed from Mount Esau,

Obadiah 1:10.text: because of the slaughter and the impiety toward your brother Jacob; and shame will cover you, and you will be removed forever.

Obadiah 1:11.text: From the day you stood opposed, on the day foreigners took his strength captive and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.

Obadiah 1:12.text: Do not look on your brother’s day, on the day of strangers; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their destruction; do not speak boastfully on the day of affliction.

Obadiah 1:13.text: Do not enter the gates of peoples on the day of their suffering. You, too, must not look on their assembly on the day of their destruction, and do not join in attacking their strength on the day of their destruction.

Obadiah 1:14.text: Do not stand at their escape routes to destroy those of them who are being saved, and do not shut in those fleeing from them on the day of affliction.

Obadiah 1:15.text: For the day of the Lord is near against all the nations. Just as you acted, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your own head.

Obadiah 1:16.text: For just as you drank on My holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though they did not exist.

Obadiah 1:17.text: But on Mount Zion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; the house of Jacob will possess those who possessed them.

Obadiah 1:18.text: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will blaze against them and consume them, and there will be no bearer of fire in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.

Obadiah 1:19.text: Those in the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those in the Shephelah will possess the foreigners. They will possess the mountain of Ephraim, the plain of Samaria, Benjamin and the land of Gilead.

Obadiah 1:20.text: And this is the beginning of the deportation: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the deportation of Jerusalem as far as Ephrathah. They will inherit the cities of the Negeb.

Obadiah 1:21.text: And men who have been saved shall ascend from Mount Zion to execute judgment upon the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

Zephaniah 2:4.text: For Gaza will be plundered and Ashkelon will disappear; Ashdod will be cast out at midday and Ekron uprooted.

Zephaniah 2:5.text: Woe to the seacoast’s inhabitants, sojourners of Cretans! The Lord’s word is against you, Canaan, land of foreigners: I will destroy you from your dwelling.

Zephaniah 2:6.text: Crete will become pasture for flocks and an enclosure for sheep,

Zephaniah 2:7.text: and the seacoast will belong to the remnant of Judah’s house. They will graze upon them in Ashkelon’s houses; at evening they will lodge away from the sons of Judah, for the Lord their God has visited them and turned their captivity.

Zephaniah 2:8.text: I heard Moab’s reproaches and the Ammonites’ blows, with which they reproached My people and exalted themselves against My borders.

Zephaniah 2:9.text: Therefore, as I live, says the Lord of powers, the God of Israel, Moab will be like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah, and Damascus abandoned like a heap on a threshing floor and vanished forever. My people’s remnant will plunder them; My nation’s remnant will inherit them.

Zephaniah 2:10.text: This will be theirs for their arrogance, because they reproached and exalted themselves against the Lord Almighty.

Zephaniah 2:11.text: The Lord will appear against them and destroy all the gods of the nations of the earth. All the islands of the nations will worship Him, each from his place.

Zephaniah 2:12.text: You too, Ethiopians, are slain by My sword.

Zephaniah 2:13.text: He will stretch His hand against the north and destroy the Assyrian, making Nineveh a waterless wasteland like a wilderness.

Zephaniah 2:14.text: Flocks and all the wild animals of the earth will graze within her; chameleons and hedgehogs will lie in her recessed panels. Wild animals will cry in her openings, and ravens in her gateways, for cedar is her structure.

Zephaniah 2:15.text: This is the contemptuous city dwelling in confidence, saying in her heart, “I am, and there is no one after me.” How she became a wasteland, pasture for wild animals! Everyone passing through her will hiss and wave his hands.

Psalms 78:1.text: A psalm for Asaph. God, nations entered Thine inheritance; they defiled Thy holy temple; they made Jerusalem into a fruit-watchman’s hut.

Psalms 78:2.text: They made the dead bodies of Thy servants food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of Thy holy ones for the beasts of the earth.

Psalms 78:3.text: They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.

Psalms 78:4.text: We became a reproach to our neighbors, sneering and ridicule to those around us.

Deuteronomy 4:5.text: Behold, I have shown you ordinances and judgments, as the Lord commanded me, that you should do so in the land whither you go to inherit it.

Deuteronomy 4:6.text: And you shall keep and do them; for this is your wisdom and understanding before all the nations, who shall hear all these ordinances and say: Behold, this great nation is a wise and understanding people.

Deuteronomy 4:7.text: For what great nation is there whose god draws near unto them, as the Lord our God in all things wherein we call upon Him?

Deuteronomy 4:8.text: And what great nation is there that has ordinances and judgments as righteous as all this law which I set before you this day?

Lamentations 2:13.text: What can I testify to you, or what can I liken to you, Daughter Jerusalem? Who will save you and comfort you, virgin Daughter Zion? For the cup of your crushing has grown great; who will heal you?

Lamentations 2:14.text: Your prophets saw futile things and folly for you. They did not uncover your injustice to turn back your captivity; they saw for you futile pronouncements and expulsions.

Lamentations 2:15.text: All who pass along the road clapped their hands at you. They hissed and shook their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: “Is this the city they will call a crown of glory, the gladness of all the earth?”

Lamentations 2:16.text: All your enemies opened their mouths against you. They hissed and gnashed their teeth; they said, “We have swallowed her! Indeed, this is the day we expected; we found it, we saw it!”

Lamentations 2:17.text: The Lord did what He intended; He fulfilled His words, which He commanded from ancient days. He brought down without sparing; He made the enemy rejoice over you and exalted your oppressor’s horn.

Ezekiel 21:33.text: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord concerning the sons of Ammon and their reproach.’ Say, ‘Sword, sword, drawn for victims and drawn for complete destruction, arise so that you may gleam,

Ezekiel 21:34.text: in your vain vision and your divining false things, to hand you over upon the necks of the wounded lawless, whose day has arrived in a season of injustice—an end!

Ezekiel 21:35.text: Turn back; do not lodge in this place where you were born. In your own land I will judge you

Ezekiel 21:36.text: and pour My anger upon you. I will blow upon you with the fire of My anger and hand you into the hands of barbarian men devising destruction.

Ezekiel 21:37.text: You will be food in fire; your blood will be in the midst of your land. There certainly will be no remembrance of you, for I, the Lord, have spoken.’”

Isaiah 23:1.text: The vision of Tyre. Wail, ships of Carthage, because she has perished, and they no longer come from the Kitians’ land; she has been led captive.

Isaiah 23:2.text: Whom have the island-dwelling traders of Phoenicia become like, crossing the sea

Isaiah 23:3.text: upon much water, seed of traders? Like a harvest being brought in are the nations’ traders.

Isaiah 23:4.text: “Be ashamed, Sidon,” said the sea; and the sea’s strength said, “I did not labor or give birth or rear young men or raise maidens.”

Isaiah 23:5.text: When it becomes known to Egypt, pain will seize them concerning Tyre.

Isaiah 23:6.text: Go away to Carthage! Wail, residents of this island!

Isaiah 23:7.text: Was this not your insolence from the beginning, before she was handed over?

Isaiah 23:8.text: Who planned these things against Tyre? Is she weaker, or has she no strength? Her merchants are glorious, rulers of the earth.

Isaiah 23:9.text: The Lord Sabaoth planned it, to dissolve all the insolence of the glorious and dishonor everything glorious upon the earth.

Isaiah 23:10.text: Work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage.

Isaiah 23:11.text: Your hand no longer has strength at sea, the hand that provoked kings. The Lord Sabaoth commanded concerning Canaan, to destroy her strength.

Isaiah 23:12.text: They will say, “You shall no longer continue in insolence and in wronging Sidon’s daughter.” Even if you go to the Kitians, there too you will have no rest,

Isaiah 23:13.text: and into the Chaldeans’ land: this too has been devastated by the Assyrians. There too you will have no rest, because her wall has fallen.

Isaiah 23:14.text: Wail, ships of Carthage, because your fortress has perished!

Isaiah 23:15.text: On that day Tyre will be left for seventy years, like a king’s time, like a person’s time. After seventy years, Tyre will be like a prostitute’s song:

Isaiah 23:16.text: “Take a lyre, wander through cities, forgotten prostitute! Play the lyre well, sing much, so that you may be remembered.”

Isaiah 23:17.text: After seventy years God will visit Tyre, and she will again be restored to her former state and become a trading center for all the inhabited world’s kingdoms.

Isaiah 23:18.text: Her trade and her wage will be holy to the Lord. It will not be collected for them; instead, all her trade will be for those dwelling before the Lord, to eat and drink and be filled, as a contribution, a memorial before the Lord.

Isaiah 17:12.text: Woe, the multitude of many nations! Like a surging sea, so you will be troubled, and the back of many nations will roar like water.

Isaiah 17:13.text: Many nations are like abundant water, like much water violently rushing down. He will drive him away and pursue him far off, like chaff-dust when people winnow before wind, and like wheel-dust carried by a squall.

Isaiah 17:14.text: Toward evening there will be mourning; before morning it will be gone. This is the portion of those who plundered you, an inheritance for those who took possession of you.

Daniel 2:1.text: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, the king fell into visions and dreams and was disturbed in his dream, and his sleep left him.

Daniel 2:36.text: This was the vision; now we will state its interpretation before the king.

Daniel 2:37.text: You, O king, are king of kings, and the Lord of heaven has given you rule, kingdom, strength, honor, and glory.

Daniel 2:38.text: Throughout the inhabited world He has handed over into your hands human beings, wild beasts, birds of heaven, and fish of the sea, to rule them all. You are the golden head.

2 Kings 25:1.text: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came with all his force against Jerusalem. He camped against it and built an enclosing wall against it all around.

2 Kings 25:2.text: The city remained under siege until King Sedekias’s eleventh year.

2 Kings 25:3.text: On the ninth of the month the famine grew severe in the city, and there were no loaves for the people of the land.

2 Kings 25:4.text: The city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night by way of the gate between the walls, the one belonging to the king’s garden, with the Chaldeans surrounding the city. He went by the way of the Araba.

Jeremiah 8:13.text: and they will gather their produce, says the Lord. There is no grape on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.

Jeremiah 8:14.text: Why are we sitting? Gather, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and made us drink gall-water, because we sinned before Him.

Jeremiah 8:15.text: We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste!

Jeremiah 8:16.text: From Dan we will hear the shrill sound of his horses; at the sound of the neighing of his riding horses the whole earth shook. And he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.

Jeremiah 8:17.text: Because behold, I am sending out among you deadly snakes that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you.

Isaiah 24:7.text: Wine will mourn, the vine will mourn, and all who gladden the soul will groan.

Isaiah 24:8.text: The joy of tambourines has ceased; the impudence and wealth of the ungodly have ceased; the lyre’s sound has ceased.

Isaiah 24:9.text: They were ashamed and did not drink wine; sikera became bitter to those drinking it.

Isaiah 24:10.text: Every city was deserted; he will shut a house so that none may enter.

Isaiah 24:11.text: Wail over wine everywhere! All the earth’s gladness has ceased.

Isaiah 24:12.text: Cities will be left deserted, and abandoned houses will perish.

Jonah 3:1.text: The word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying:

Jonah 3:2.text: “Rise and go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim in it according to the former proclamation that I spoke to you.”

Jonah 3:3.text: Jonah rose and went to Nineveh as the Lord had spoken. Now Nineveh was a city great before God, about a three-day journey.

Jonah 3:4.text: And Jonah began to enter the city, about a day’s journey, and he proclaimed and said, “Three more days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown.”

Jonah 3:5.text: The people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their greatest to their least.

Jonah 3:6.text: The word reached the king of Nineveh. He rose from his throne, took his robe off himself, wrapped himself in sackcloth and sat in ashes.

Jonah 3:7.text: It was proclaimed and declared in Nineveh from the king and his nobles: “Let people and livestock, cattle and sheep, taste nothing; let them not graze or drink water.”

Jonah 3:8.text: People and livestock clothed themselves in sackcloth, and they cried earnestly to God. Each turned away from his evil way and from the injustice in their hands, saying:

Jonah 3:9.text: “Who knows whether God will relent and turn from His fierce anger, so that we certainly do not perish?”

Jonah 3:10.text: God saw their deeds, that they had turned from their evil ways. God relented concerning the calamity He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.

Jeremiah 28:41.text: How the boast of the whole earth was captured and hunted! How Babylon became a ruin among the nations!

Jeremiah 28:42.text: The sea rose over Babylon with the sound of its waves, and she was covered.

Jeremiah 28:43.text: Her cities became a waterless and untrodden land; not one person will live there, nor will any human lodge there.

Jeremiah 28:44.text: I will exact vengeance on Babylon and bring what she swallowed out of her mouth. Nations will certainly no longer gather to her.

Isaiah 14:4.text: and you will take up this lament against Babylon’s king and say on that day, “How the one who made demands has rested, and the taskmaster rested!

Isaiah 14:5.text: God shattered the sinners’ yoke, the rulers’ yoke;

Isaiah 14:6.text: having struck a nation in wrath with an incurable blow, striking a nation with a blow of anger that did not spare,

Isaiah 14:7.text: he rested confidently. The whole earth cries out with gladness,

Isaiah 14:8.text: and Lebanon’s trees rejoiced over you, and Lebanon’s cedar: ‘Since you have fallen asleep, the one cutting us has not come up.’

Isaiah 14:9.text: Hades below grew bitter on meeting you. All the giants who ruled the earth rose together for you, those who raised all the nations’ kings from their thrones.

Isaiah 14:10.text: They will all answer and say to you, ‘You too were captured as we were, and were numbered among us.’

Isaiah 14:11.text: Your glory went down to Hades, your abundant gladness. They will spread decay beneath you, and your covering is a worm.

Isaiah 14:12.text: How the dawn-bearer who rises in the morning fell from heaven! The one dispatching to all the nations was shattered to earth.

Isaiah 14:13.text: You said in your mind, ‘I will ascend to heaven, set my throne above heaven’s stars, and sit on a high mountain, upon the high mountains toward the north.

Isaiah 14:14.text: I will ascend above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.’

Isaiah 14:15.text: But now you will descend to Hades and to the earth’s foundations.

Isaiah 14:16.text: Those who see you will marvel at you and say, ‘Is this the person who provoked the earth, shook kings,

Isaiah 14:17.text: who made the whole inhabited world deserted and pulled down the cities, who did not release those in captivity?’

Isaiah 14:18.text: All the nations’ kings fell asleep in honor, each in his own house;

Isaiah 14:19.text: but you will be thrown into the mountains like an abhorred dead man, with many dead pierced by swords, descending to Hades. As a garment stained with blood will not be clean,

Isaiah 14:20.text: so neither will you be clean, because you destroyed My land and killed My people. You will certainly not endure for everlasting time, evil offspring.

Isaiah 14:21.text: Prepare your children to be slaughtered because of your father’s sins, so that they do not rise, inherit the earth and fill the earth with cities.”

Isaiah 14:22.text: “I will rise against them,” says the Lord Sabaoth, “and destroy their name, remnant and offspring”—thus says the Lord—

Isaiah 14:23.text: “and make Babylonia deserted, so that hedgehogs dwell there; she will become nothing. I will make her a muddy abyss for destruction.”

Ezekiel 47:6.text: He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man?” Then he led me to the river’s edge.

Ezekiel 47:7.text: As I returned, look—very many trees were on the river’s edge, on both sides.

Ezekiel 47:8.text: He said to me, “This water flowing out into eastern Galilee was descending into Arabia and coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet; it will heal the waters.

Ezekiel 47:9.text: Every life among the swarming living creatures will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because this water has arrived there, and it will become healthy and live. Everything over which the river comes will live.

Ezekiel 47:10.text: Fishers will stand there from Aingadin to Ainagalim; there will be a drying place for nets. It will be by itself, and its fish will be like the fish of the Great Sea, an exceedingly great multitude.

Ezekiel 47:11.text: At its outlet, at its turning, and at its overflow, they will certainly not be healed; they are given over to salt.

Ezekiel 47:12.text: Along the river, on its edge on both sides, every edible tree will grow. Nothing upon it will grow old, nor will its fruit fail. In its newness it will bear its first crop, because these waters flow from the holy places. Their fruit will be for food and their growth for health.

Amos 2:1.text: Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away from him, because they burned the bones of Idumea’s king into lime.

Amos 2:2.text: I will send fire upon Moab, and it will devour the foundations of her cities. Moab will die in weakness, with shouting and the sound of a trumpet.

Amos 2:3.text: I will destroy the judge from her, and kill all her rulers with him,” says the Lord.

Nahum 3:1.text: O city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice! Prey will not be touched.

Nahum 3:2.text: The sound of whips and the sound of shaking wheels, of a pursuing horse and a jolting chariot,

Nahum 3:3.text: and of a mounting horseman, a flashing sword and glittering weapons, a multitude of slain and a grievous fall! There was no limit to her nations, and they will weaken in their bodies

Nahum 3:4.text: because of the multitude of prostitution. A prostitute, beautiful and pleasing, mistress of potions, selling nations through her prostitution and tribes through her potions,

Nahum 3:5.text: look, I am against you, says the Lord God Almighty. I will expose your hind parts over your face and show nations your shame and kingdoms your dishonor,

Nahum 3:6.text: and cast abomination upon you according to your impurities, and make you an example,

Nahum 3:7.text: and everyone seeing you will spring away and say, “Miserable Nineveh! Who will lament her? Where shall I seek consolation for her?”

Jeremiah 31:20.text: Moab was ashamed, for he was shattered. Wail and cry out; announce at Arnon that Moab perished.

Jeremiah 31:21.text: Judgment is coming into the land of Misor: upon Chailon, Jahzah, and Mophath,

Jeremiah 31:22.text: upon Dibon, Nebo, and the house of Deblathaim,

Jeremiah 31:23.text: upon Kiriathaim, the house of Gamol, and the house of Maon,

Jeremiah 31:24.text: upon Kerioth, Bosor, and all Moab’s cities, far and near.

Jeremiah 31:25.text: Moab’s horn was broken and his effort shattered.

Jeremiah 31:26.text: Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the Lord. Moab will strike with his hand and become a laughingstock himself.

Jeremiah 31:27.text: Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he found in your thefts, that you made war on him?

Daniel 2:24.text: Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to kill all Babylonia’s learned men, and said, “Do not destroy Babylonia’s learned men. Bring me to the king, and I will disclose every detail to him.”

Daniel 2:25.text: Then Arioch urgently brought Daniel to the king and said, “I have found a wise man from the captivity of the sons of Judea who will disclose every detail to the king.”

Daniel 2:26.text: The king answered Daniel, who was called Baltasar in Chaldean, “Will you be able to disclose to me the vision I saw and its interpretation?”

Daniel 2:27.text: Daniel spoke aloud before the king, “Disclosure of the mystery the king saw does not belong to wise men, sorcerers, incantation-singers, or gazarenes,

Daniel 2:28.text: but there is a God in heaven who uncovers mysteries, who has disclosed to King Nebuchadnezzar what must happen in the last days. O king, live for ever! This is the dream and the vision of your head upon your bed:

Daniel 2:29.text: You, O king, reclining upon your bed, saw everything that must happen in the last days, and the Revealer of mysteries disclosed to you what must happen.

Daniel 2:30.text: This mystery was revealed to me because of no wisdom in me beyond all people; rather, so that it might be disclosed to the king, what you conceived in your heart was made known to me.

1 Kings 5:15.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent his attendants to anoint Solomon in place of David his father, for Hiram had always loved David.

1 Kings 5:17.text: “You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the Lord put them beneath the footsteps of his feet.

1 Kings 5:18.text: But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side; there is no plotter and no evil encounter.

1 Kings 5:19.text: Behold, I intend to build a house for the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord God told my father David: ‘Your son, whom I shall place on your throne in your place, shall build the house for My name.’

1 Kings 5:20.text: Now command that they cut timber from Lebanon for me. Behold, my servants are with your servants, and I will pay you the wages of your service according to whatever you say; for you know that no one among us knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.”

1 Kings 5:21.text: When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be God this day, who has given David a discerning son over this great people!”

1 Kings 5:22.text: He sent to Solomon, saying, “I have heard about everything you did send to me. I will fulfill all your wishes: cedar and pine timber.

1 Kings 5:23.text: My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea. I will make them into rafts as far as the place you send me word about, and shake them apart there; you shall take them away. You shall fulfill my wish by providing loaves for my household.”

1 Kings 5:24.text: Hiram supplied Solomon with cedars and all that he desired.

1 Kings 5:25.text: Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat and machir for his household, and twenty thousand beth of beaten oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram each year.
