1 Kings 10:29.text: The export from Egypt came up: a chariot for a hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for fifty pieces of silver. In this way they went out by sea for all the Hittite kings and the kings of Syria.

Isaiah 27:1.text: On that day God will bring the holy, great and strong sword against the dragon, the fleeing serpent, against the dragon, the crooked serpent, and will kill the dragon.

Isaiah 27:2.text: On that day, a beautiful vineyard; a desire to lead a song against her.

Isaiah 27:3.text: “I am a strong city, a besieged city; in vain I will water her, for she will be captured by night, and by day the wall will fall.

Isaiah 27:4.text: There is none who has not seized her. Who will set me to guard stubble in a field? Because of this hostility I rejected her.” Therefore, for this reason the Lord God has done everything He commanded. “I have been burned!”

Isaiah 27:5.text: the residents in her will cry. “Let us make peace with Him; let us make peace.”

Isaiah 27:6.text: Those coming, Jacob’s children—Israel will sprout and flower, and the inhabited world will be filled with his fruit.

Job 40:1.text: The Lord God answered Job and said:

Job 40:2.text: “Will he evade judgment with the Mighty One? Will the one reproving God answer it?”

Job 40:3.text: Then Job replied to the Lord:

Job 40:4.text: “Why am I still being judged, being admonished and reproving the Lord, hearing such things though I am nothing? What answer can I give to these things? I will place a hand over my mouth;

Job 40:5.text: I have spoken once, but a second time I will add nothing.”

Job 40:6.text: Again the Lord replied to Job from the cloud:

Job 40:7.text: “No, but gird your waist like a man; I will question you, and you must answer Me.

Job 40:8.text: Do not reject My judgment. Do you think I have dealt with you for any other purpose than that you may be shown righteous?

Job 40:25.text: Will you bring a dragon with a hook and place a muzzle around its nose?

Job 40:26.text: Will you fasten a ring in its nostril and pierce its lip with a band?

Job 40:27.text: Will it speak to you with a plea, softly with supplication?

Job 40:28.text: Will it establish a covenant with you, and will you take it as an everlasting slave?

Job 40:29.text: Will you play with it like a bird, or tie it like a little bird for a child?

Job 40:30.text: Will nations feed upon it, and will Phoenician clans divide it?

Job 40:31.text: All floating craft gathered together certainly cannot carry one hide from its tail, nor its head in fishermen’s boats.

Job 40:32.text: Will you lay a hand upon it, remembering the war taking place within its body? Let it happen no more.”

Jeremiah 7:32.text: Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say Topheth’s Altar or Ravine of the Son of Hinnom, but Ravine of the Slain; and they will bury in Topheth because there is no space.

Jeremiah 7:33.text: And this people’s dead will be food for heaven’s birds and the earth’s wild beasts, and there will be no one to drive them off.

Jeremiah 7:34.text: And I will stop the sound of those rejoicing and the sound of those glad, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, from Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s thoroughfares, because the whole land will become a desolation.

Isaiah 36:2.text: The king of the Assyrians sent Rapsakes from Lachis to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large force. He stood at the upper pool’s aqueduct, on the road of the fuller’s field.

Isaiah 36:3.text: Eliakim son of Chelkias, the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joach son of Asaph, the record-keeper, went out to him.

Isaiah 36:4.text: Rapsakes said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: ‘What do you trust in?

Isaiah 36:5.text: Does a battle line arise through counsel or words of lips? Now whom have you trusted, that you disobey me?

Isaiah 36:6.text: Behold, you trust this broken reed staff, Egypt. Whoever leans on it, it will enter his hand. Such are Pharaoh king of Egypt and all who trust in him.

Ezekiel 14:12.text: The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

Ezekiel 14:13.text: “Son of man, if a land sins against Me by committing a transgression, and I stretch My hand against it, shatter its support of bread, send famine upon it, and remove human and livestock from it,

Ezekiel 14:14.text: even if these three men—Noah, Daniel and Job—were within it, they themselves would be saved by their righteousness, says the Lord.

Ezekiel 14:15.text: Even if I bring evil beasts upon the land and punish it, so that it becomes a devastation and no one passes through because of the beasts,

Ezekiel 14:16.text: and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be saved; only they themselves would be saved, and the land would be destroyed.

Ezekiel 14:17.text: Or even if I bring a sword upon that land and say, ‘Let a sword pass through the land,’ and remove human and livestock from it,

Ezekiel 14:18.text: and these three men were within it, as I live, says the Lord, they certainly would not rescue sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.

Ezekiel 14:19.text: Or even if I send death upon that land and pour My wrath upon it in blood, to destroy human and livestock from it,

Ezekiel 14:20.text: and Noah, Daniel and Job were within it, as I live, says the Lord, neither sons nor daughters would be left; they would rescue their own lives by their righteousness.

Ezekiel 14:21.text: Thus says the Lord: Even if I send My four evil retributions—sword, famine, evil beasts and death—against Jerusalem, to destroy human and livestock from her,

Isaiah 30:1.text: “Woe, rebellious children,” thus says the Lord, “you made a plan not through Me and agreements not through My spirit, to add sins upon sins,

Isaiah 30:2.text: you who go down to Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and sheltered by Egyptians.

Isaiah 30:3.text: For Pharaoh’s shelter will become your shame, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.

Isaiah 30:4.text: For there are leaders in Tanis, evil messengers; they will labor in vain

Isaiah 30:5.text: toward a people that will not benefit them, neither for assistance nor for profit, but for shame and reproach.”

Isaiah 31:1.text: Woe to those going down to Egypt for help, trusting in horses and chariots because there are many, and in horses, a very great multitude, but not trusting Israel’s Holy One or seeking God!

Isaiah 31:2.text: He Himself, wise, brought evils upon them; His word will certainly not be set aside. He will rise against evil people’s houses and against their futile hope,

Isaiah 31:3.text: an Egyptian human being and not God, horses’ flesh, with no help. The Lord will bring His hand against them; the helpers will grow weary, and all will perish together.

Jeremiah 26:11.text: Go up, Gilead, and take resin for the virgin daughter Egypt. In vain you multiplied your remedies; there is no benefit for you.

Jeremiah 26:12.text: Nations heard your voice, and the land was filled with your cry, for warrior grew weak against warrior; both fell together.

Jeremiah 26:13.text: What the Lord spoke through Jeremiah concerning Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon coming to cut down Egypt’s land:

Jeremiah 26:14.text: Announce to Migdol and proclaim to Memphis. Say, Take your position and prepare, for the sword has devoured your smilax growth.

Jeremiah 26:2.text: For Egypt, concerning the force of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, who was beside the Euphrates River at Carchemish and whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim king of Judah:

Jeremiah 26:3.text: Take up weapons and shields, and advance to war!

Jeremiah 26:4.text: Saddle the horses; mount, riders! Take your positions in your helmets. Hold your spears forward; put on your breastplates!

Jeremiah 50:1.text: When Jeremiah stopped speaking to the people all the Lord’s words, with which the Lord had sent him to them—all these words—

Jeremiah 50:2.text: Azariah son of Maaseiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the men who spoke said to Jeremiah, You are lying! The Lord did not send you to us to say, Do not enter Egypt to live there.

Jeremiah 50:3.text: Rather, Baruch son of Neriah is setting you against us, so that you will hand us over to the Chaldeans, to put us to death and have us deported to Babylon.

Jeremiah 50:4.text: Johanan, all the commanders of the force, and all the people did not obey the Lord’s voice by remaining in Judah’s land.

Jeremiah 50:5.text: Johanan and all the commanders of the force took all Judah’s survivors who had returned to live in the land:

Jeremiah 50:6.text: the mighty men, the women, the little children, the king’s daughters, the people Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.

Jeremiah 50:7.text: They entered Egypt, for they had not obeyed the Lord’s voice. They entered Taphnas.

Jeremiah 50:8.text: The Lord’s word came to Jeremiah at Taphnas:

Jeremiah 50:9.text: Take large stones for yourself and hide them in the forecourt at the gate of Pharaoh’s house at Taphnas, before the eyes of Judah’s men.

Jeremiah 50:10.text: Say, Thus said the Lord: I am sending and will bring Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will place his throne above these stones that you hid and raise his weapons over them.

Jeremiah 50:11.text: He will enter and strike Egypt’s land: those for death, to death; those for deportation, to deportation; and those for the sword, to the sword.

Jeremiah 50:12.text: He will kindle fire in the houses of their gods, burn the houses, and deport the gods. He will delouse Egypt’s land as a shepherd delouses his garment, and he will go out in peace.

Jeremiah 50:13.text: He will shatter the pillars of the City of the Sun, those in On, and burn their houses with fire.

Psalms 131:11.text: The Lord swore truth to David, and He will certainly not annul it: “From the fruit of your belly I will set one on your throne.

Psalms 131:12.text: If your sons keep My covenant and these testimonies of Mine that I will teach them, their sons too will sit for ever on your throne.”

Psalms 131:13.text: For the Lord chose Zion; He selected her as His dwelling:

Psalms 131:14.text: “This is My rest for age upon age; here I will dwell, for I selected her.

Psalms 131:15.text: I will surely bless her game; I will satisfy her poor with loaves.

Psalms 131:16.text: I will clothe her priests with salvation, and her holy ones will surely exult.

Psalms 131:17.text: There I will make a horn spring up for David; I have prepared a lamp for My anointed.

Psalms 131:18.text: I will clothe his enemies with shame, but upon him My holy sign will blossom.”

Ezekiel 24:25.text: And you, son of man, will it not be on the day when I take their strength from them, the exaltation of their boasting, the desires of their eyes, the exaltation of their soul, their sons and daughters—

Ezekiel 24:26.text: on that day the survivor will come to you to announce it into your ears?

Ezekiel 24:27.text: On that day your mouth will be opened toward the survivor; you will speak and certainly will no longer be struck mute. You will be a portent for them, and they will recognize that I am the Lord.’”

Joel 1:13.text: Wrap yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, ministers of the altar! Enter and sleep in sackcloth, ministers of God, because sacrifice and drink offering have been kept away from your God’s house.

Joel 1:14.text: Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service. Gather elders, all who inhabit the land, into your God’s house, and cry earnestly to the Lord,

Joel 1:15.text: “Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”

Joel 1:16.text: Before your eyes food was destroyed, and gladness and joy from your God’s house.

Joel 1:17.text: Heifers leaped at their feeding troughs; storehouses disappeared, winepresses were demolished, because grain dried up.

Joel 1:18.text: What shall we store up for ourselves? Herds of cattle wept because they had no pasture, and flocks of sheep disappeared.

Joel 1:19.text: To Thee, Lord, I will cry, because fire consumed the beautiful places of the wilderness, and flame kindled all the field’s trees.

Joel 1:20.text: Even the animals of the plain looked up toward Thee, because outlets of water dried up, and fire devoured the beautiful places of the wilderness.

Isaiah 13:1.text: The vision that Isaiah son of Amos saw against Babylon.

Isaiah 13:2.text: Raise a signal on a level mountain, lift your voice to them, do not fear, beckon with the hand: “Open, rulers!”

Isaiah 13:3.text: I command, and I lead them; they are consecrated, and I lead them. Giants are coming to fulfill My wrath, rejoicing and acting insolently together.

Isaiah 13:4.text: A sound of many nations upon the mountains, like many nations; a sound of kings and gathered nations. The Lord Sabaoth has commanded an armed nation,

Isaiah 13:5.text: to come from a distant land, from the farthest edge of heaven’s foundation—the Lord and His armed fighters—to destroy the whole inhabited world.

Isaiah 13:6.text: Wail, for the Lord’s day is near, and shattering will come from God.

Isaiah 13:7.text: Therefore every hand will slacken, and every human soul grow cowardly;

Isaiah 13:8.text: the envoys will be troubled, and labor pains will hold them like those of a woman giving birth. They will lament to one another and be distraught, and change their face as to flame.

Isaiah 13:9.text: For behold, the Lord’s incurable day comes, of wrath and anger, to make the whole inhabited world deserted and destroy its sinners from it.

Isaiah 13:10.text: For heaven’s stars, Orion and all heaven’s array will not give light; it will grow dark as the sun rises, and the moon will not give its light.

Isaiah 13:11.text: I will ordain evils for the whole inhabited world, and for the ungodly their sins; I will destroy the insolence of the lawless and lower the insolence of the proud.

Isaiah 13:12.text: Those left will be more precious than unrefined gold, and a human being more precious than the stone from Souphir.

Isaiah 13:13.text: For heaven will be enraged, and the earth shaken from its foundations through the fury of the Lord Sabaoth’s anger, on the day when His wrath comes upon it.

Isaiah 20:1.text: In the year Tanathan entered Azotus, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians and fought Azotus and seized it,

Isaiah 20:2.text: then the Lord spoke to Isaiah, saying, “Go, remove the sackcloth from your waist and untie the sandals on your feet.” He did so, going naked and without sandals.

Isaiah 20:3.text: The Lord said, “As Isaiah My servant has gone naked and without sandals for three years, there will be signs and wonders for the Egyptians and Ethiopians;

Isaiah 20:4.text: for thus the king of the Assyrians will lead Egypt’s and the Ethiopians’ captivity, young men and elders, naked and without sandals, exposed as Egypt’s shame.

Isaiah 20:5.text: The Egyptians will be ashamed in defeat because of the Ethiopians, in whom the Egyptians had trusted, for they were their glory.

Isaiah 20:6.text: Those dwelling on this island will say, ‘Behold, we had trusted that we could flee to them for help, but they could not be saved from the king of the Assyrians. How, then, shall we be saved?’”

Exodus 7:1.text: And the Lord said to Moses, “Behold, I have made you a god to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.

Exodus 7:2.text: You shall speak to him all that I command you; and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he may let the sons of Israel go out of his land.

Exodus 7:3.text: I will harden Pharaoh’s heart and multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.

Exodus 7:4.text: Pharaoh will not listen to you. I will lay My hand on Egypt and bring out My people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with My power and great vengeance.

Exodus 7:5.text: All the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when I stretch out My hand over Egypt and bring the sons of Israel out from among them.”

Exodus 10:21.text: And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let there be darkness upon the land of Egypt, darkness that may be felt.”

Exodus 10:22.text: Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was darkness, gloom, and a tempest throughout the land of Egypt for three days.

Exodus 10:23.text: No one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose from his bed for three days. But all the sons of Israel had light everywhere they lived.

Exodus 12:12.text: I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.

Exodus 12:13.text: And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.

Isaiah 19:1.text: A vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud and will come into Egypt; Egypt’s handmade objects will be shaken before Him, and their heart overcome within them.

Isaiah 19:2.text: Egyptians will be roused against Egyptians; each will fight his brother and each his neighbor, city against city and district against district.

Isaiah 19:3.text: The Egyptians’ spirit will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel. They will inquire of their gods, their statues, those speaking from the earth and the belly-speakers.

Isaiah 19:4.text: I will hand Egypt into the hands of harsh human masters, and harsh kings will rule them. Thus says the Lord Sabaoth.

Isaiah 19:5.text: The Egyptians will drink water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up.

Isaiah 19:6.text: Rivers and the river’s canals will fail, and every gathering of water dry up, in every marsh of reed and papyrus,

Isaiah 19:7.text: and all the green marsh growth around the river and everything sown by the river will dry up, destroyed by wind.

Isaiah 19:8.text: Fishermen will groan, and all casting a hook into the river will groan; those casting seines and those using casting nets will mourn.

Isaiah 19:9.text: Shame will seize those working split flax and those working fine linen,

Isaiah 19:10.text: and those warping them will be in pain, and all who make beer will be grieved and suffer in their souls.

Isaiah 19:11.text: Tanis’s rulers will be fools; the king’s wise counselors—their counsel will become foolish. How will you say to the king, “We are sons of the discerning, sons of kings from the beginning”?

Isaiah 19:12.text: Where are your wise men now? Let them announce to you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has counseled against Egypt.

Isaiah 19:13.text: Tanis’s rulers failed, and Memphis’s rulers were exalted; they will lead Egypt astray tribe by tribe.

Isaiah 19:14.text: For the Lord mixed for them a spirit of wandering; they led Egypt astray in all their works, as someone wanders while drunk and vomiting.

Isaiah 19:15.text: There will be no work for the Egyptians that will produce a head and tail, a beginning and end.

Isaiah 10:5.text: Woe to the Assyrians! The rod of My anger and wrath is in their hands.

Isaiah 10:6.text: I will send My anger against a lawless nation, and I will command My people to take spoils and plunder, trample the cities and reduce them to dust.

Isaiah 10:7.text: But he did not consider it this way and has not reckoned it this way in his soul; rather, his mind will turn aside, even to destroy not a few nations.

Daniel 4:4.text: In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, he said, “I was at peace in my house and prospering upon my throne.

Daniel 4:5.text: I saw a dream and became apprehensive; fear fell upon me.

Daniel 4:10.text: I was sleeping, and there was a tall tree growing upon the earth. Its appearance was great, and no other was like it.

Daniel 4:11.text: Its appearance was great: its top reached to heaven, and its mass to the clouds, filling what lay beneath heaven. The sun and moon dwelt in it and illuminated the whole earth.

Daniel 4:12.text: Its branches were about thirty stadia long. All the wild animals of the earth found shade beneath it, and the birds of heaven nested in it. Its fruit was abundant and good, and it supplied all living creatures.

Daniel 4:13.text: I was watching in my sleep, and an angel was sent in strength from heaven.

Daniel 4:14.text: He called out and said to it, ‘Cut it down and destroy it, for the Most High has commanded that it be uprooted and rendered useless.’

Daniel 4:15.text: He spoke in this way: ‘Leave one root of it in the earth, so that it may graze on grass like an ox with the wild animals of the earth in the mountains;

Daniel 4:16.text: let his body be changed by heaven’s dew, and let him graze with them for seven years,

Daniel 4:17.text: until he knows that the Lord of heaven has authority over everything in heaven and upon earth, and does among them whatever He wills.’

Daniel 4:17a.text: Before me it was cut down in one day, and its destruction came within one hour of the day. Its branches were given to every wind; it was dragged away and thrown down. It ate the grass of the earth with the wild animals of the earth, was handed over to custody, and was bound by them in fetters and bronze handcuffs. I was greatly astonished at all this, and sleep departed from my eyes.

Daniel 4:18.text: In the morning I rose from my bed and called Daniel, chief of the learned experts and leader of those who judge dreams. I recounted the dream to him, and he explained its entire interpretation to me.

Daniel 4:19.text: Daniel was greatly astonished, and apprehension pressed upon him. Frightened, seized with trembling, and changed in appearance, he shook his head and remained astonished for an hour. He answered me in a gentle voice, ‘O king, may this dream come upon those who hate you and its interpretation upon your enemies!

Daniel 4:20.text: You, O king, are the tree planted in the earth, whose appearance was great.

Daniel 4:21.text: And all the birds of heaven nesting in it—the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all languages to the ends of the earth, and all countries—serve you.

Daniel 4:22.text: The raising of that tree, its reaching heaven, and its mass touching the clouds mean that you, O king, were raised above all people upon the face of the whole earth. Your heart was raised in pride and strength against the Holy One and His angels. Your deeds were seen, because you laid waste the house of the living God on account of the sins of the consecrated people.

Daniel 4:23.text: The vision you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord and commanded the tree’s removal and cutting down, means that the judgment of the great God will come upon you,

Daniel 4:24.text: and the Most High and His angels are rushing against you.

Daniel 4:25.text: They will lead you away into custody and send you to a deserted place.

Daniel 4:26.text: The root of the tree that was left, since it was not uprooted, means that the place of your throne will be preserved for you for a time and an hour. Behold! They are preparing against you; they will scourge you and bring the judgments upon you.

Daniel 4:27.text: The Lord lives in heaven, and His authority is over all the earth. Entreat Him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices by almsgiving, so that gentleness may be granted you, you may have many days upon your royal throne, and He may not destroy you. Love these words, for my word is accurate and your time is full.’”

Daniel 4:28.text: At the completion of the words, Nebuchadnezzar, when he heard the judgment of the vision, kept the words in his heart.

Daniel 4:29.text: After twelve months, the king was walking upon the city walls with all his glory and passing over its towers.

Daniel 4:30.text: He spoke and said, “This is great Babylon, which I built, and it will be called the house of my kingship through the strength of my might, for the honor of my glory.”

Daniel 4:31.text: At the completion of his word, he heard a voice from heaven: “To you it is said, King Nebuchadnezzar: Babylon’s kingdom has been taken from you and is given to another, a despised man in your house. Behold! I appoint him over your kingdom; he will take your authority, glory, and luxury, so that you may recognize that the God of heaven has authority over human kingship and will give it to whomever He wishes. By sunrise another king will rejoice in your house and take possession of your glory, strength, and authority.

Daniel 4:32.text: The angels will pursue you for seven years. You will neither be seen nor speak with any human being. They will feed you grass like an ox, and your pasture will be the earth’s greenery. Behold! In place of your glory they will bind you, and another will have your luxurious house and your kingdom.

Daniel 4:33.text: By morning everything will be fulfilled upon you, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon; nothing of all this will fail.”

Daniel 4:33a.text: “I, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, was bound for seven years. They fed me grass like an ox, and I ate the earth’s greenery. After seven years I devoted my soul to supplication and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven; concerning my acts of ignorance I entreated the great God of gods.

Daniel 4:33b.text: My hair became like an eagle’s wings, and my nails like a lion’s. My flesh and my heart were changed; I walked naked with the wild animals of the earth. I saw a dream, and apprehensions seized me. After a time a deep sleep took hold of me, and drowsiness fell upon me.

Daniel 4:34.text: At the completion of the seven years, the time of my release came. My sins and my acts of ignorance reached their full measure before the God of heaven. I entreated the great God of gods concerning my acts of ignorance, and an angel called to me from heaven, saying, ‘Nebuchadnezzar, serve the holy God of heaven and give glory to the Most High; the kingship of your nation is restored to you.’

Daniel 4:36.text: At that time my kingdom was restored to me and my glory returned to me.

Daniel 4:37.text: I give thanks to the Most High and praise Him who created heaven and earth, seas and rivers, and everything in them. I give thanks and praise, for He is God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. He performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, taking kingdoms from kings and appointing others in their place.

Daniel 4:37a.text: From now on I will worship Him. Trembling has seized me through fear of Him, and I praise all His holy ones. For the gods of the nations have no strength in themselves to transfer one king’s kingdom to another king, to kill and make alive, to perform signs and great and fearsome wonders, or to change exceedingly great affairs, as the God of heaven has done in me, changing great affairs concerning me. Throughout all the days of my reign I will offer sacrifices to the Most High on behalf of my soul, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. I will do what is acceptable before Him—I and my people, my nation and my countries under my authority. Whoever has spoken against the God of heaven, and whoever is caught speaking anything against Him, I will condemn to death.”

Daniel 4:37b.text: King Nebuchadnezzar wrote a circular letter to all the nations in every place, to the countries and all languages dwelling in every country, from generation to generation: “Praise the Lord, the God of heaven, and gloriously bring Him sacrifice and offering. I, king of kings, gloriously give thanks to Him, because He has dealt with me in this way: on that very day He seated me upon my throne; I regained my authority and my kingdom among my people, and my greatness was restored to me.”

Daniel 4:37c.text: “King Nebuchadnezzar to all nations, all countries, and all who dwell in them: May peace be multiplied to you at every time. Now I will explain to you the deeds that the great God has done with me. It pleased me to demonstrate to you and to your learned experts that there is a God, and His wonders are great; His kingship is an everlasting kingship, His authority from generation to generation.” He sent letters concerning everything that had happened to him in his kingdom to all the nations under his kingship.

Jeremiah 17:5.text: Cursed is the person who places his hope in a human and will rest the flesh of his arm upon him, and whose heart departs from the Lord;

Jeremiah 17:6.text: and he will be like a wild tamarisk in the wilderness; he will not see when good things come, and will dwell among salt-plants and in a wilderness, in a salt land that is not inhabited.

Jeremiah 17:7.text: And blessed is the person who has trusted in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope;

Jeremiah 17:8.text: and he will be like a tree flourishing beside waters, and will send its roots toward moisture, and will not fear when heat comes. Wooded stems will be upon it; in a rainless year it will not fear or cease bearing fruit.

Jeremiah 17:9.text: The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?

Jeremiah 17:10.text: I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.

Isaiah 34:1.text: Draw near, nations, and hear, rulers! Let the earth and those in it hear, the inhabited world and the people in it!

Isaiah 34:2.text: For the Lord’s wrath is against all nations, and anger against their number, to destroy them and hand them over to slaughter.

Isaiah 34:3.text: Their wounded and dead will be thrown out; their odor will rise, and mountains will be soaked with their blood.
